tower-of-hanoi.title: Identify already-correct disks
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Compare the initial and goal configurations to find disks that already sit on their final peg and in the correct relative order, so they can be left untouched throughout the solution.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial state contains disks that already match their final position on the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If disk 3 is already on the goal peg with no smaller disks beneath it, you can ignore it.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Determine descending placement order
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When constructing the final stack on the goal peg, always place larger disks before any smaller ones, because the final configuration requires a descending size order from bottom to top.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When planning the sequence of moves to build the goal tower.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Place disk 5 first, then disk 4, then disk 3, and so on.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear blocking disks before moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the disk you need to move is not the topmost on its peg, first relocate every smaller disk that sits above it to an auxiliary peg, ensuring the larger disk becomes free to move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a target disk is buried under smaller disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disk 5 that has disk 2 on top, first move disk 2 elsewhere.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Use auxiliary peg for temporary storage
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When clearing blocking disks, place them on the peg that is neither the source nor the intended destination, so they do not interfere with later moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During the clearing step for a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.example: If moving a disk from peg 0 to peg 2, use peg 1 as the temporary holding spot for smaller disks.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Avoid premature placement on the goal peg
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Never move a smaller disk onto the goal peg until all larger disks that must end up below it have already been placed there, preventing the need to lift a larger disk later.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When deciding whether to move a small disk to the goal peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Do not place disk 1 on the goal peg before disks 5 and 4 are already there.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Re‑stack displaced smaller disks after larger ones
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After a larger disk has been moved to its final position on the goal peg, move the previously displaced smaller disks back onto the goal peg in the correct descending order.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After placing a larger disk on the goal peg and the temporary storage pegs are cleared.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Once disk 5 is on the goal peg, move disk 2 (which was temporarily on another peg) back onto the goal peg after disks 4 and 3 are placed.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Track top disks and legality of each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Maintain an up‑to‑date mental or written representation of each peg’s stack, updating it after every move to ensure you only move topmost disks and never place a larger disk on a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Throughout the entire solving process, before executing each move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Before moving disk 3, check that it is the top disk on its peg.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Simulate and verify final configuration
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the full move list, replay the moves from the initial state to confirm that each move is legal and that the final configuration exactly matches the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have written down the entire sequence of moves, before submitting the answer.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Run through the moves step‑by‑step; if the final peg2 stack is [5,4,3,2,1], the solution is correct.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move decomposition
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Solve a multi‑disk transfer by recursively moving the top n‑1 disks to an auxiliary peg, moving the largest disk, then moving the n‑1 disks onto the target peg, mirroring the classic Hanoi algorithm.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the problem reduces to moving a contiguous block of disks from one peg to another.
tower-of-hanoi.example: To move disks 1‑3 from peg A to peg C, first move disks 1‑2 to peg B, move disk 3 to C, then move disks 1‑2 from B to C.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Treat larger base disks on destination as fixed
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg already contains a disk larger than all disks you intend to move onto it, you can treat that larger disk as a fixed base and safely stack the remaining disks on top without moving the base disk again.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the destination peg already has the largest required disk in place.
tower-of-hanoi.example: After placing disk 5 on the goal peg, you can treat it as a permanent base while stacking disks 4‑1.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Placing a larger disk onto a smaller one
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may forget the rule that a larger disk cannot be placed on top of a smaller disk, especially when moving many disks.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always check the size of the top disk on the destination peg before moving; only move a disk if the destination is empty or its top disk is larger.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a disk that is not the topmost on its peg
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may overlook that only the top disk of a peg can be moved, leading to illegal moves.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Maintain a clear view of each peg’s stack and verify that the chosen disk is the topmost before moving.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Temporarily placing a small disk on the goal peg before a larger disk that must be below it
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may try to free a larger disk by moving a small one onto the goal peg, forgetting that the larger disk will later need to be placed underneath.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Apply the 'Avoid premature placement on the goal peg' principle: only move a small disk onto the goal peg after all larger required disks are already there.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Leaving blocking disks on the target peg when moving a larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may move a larger disk onto a peg that still has smaller disks on top, violating the rule that the larger disk must be placed on an empty peg or on a larger disk.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Before moving a larger disk, clear the destination peg of any smaller disks using the auxiliary peg.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Failing to verify that the final configuration matches the goal
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume the move list is correct without checking the final state, leading to subtle errors.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: After writing the move list, simulate the entire sequence and compare the resulting configuration with the goal.
